title: build-a-formula widget params
description: A self-contained 'compose-and-evaluate' engine for first-order satisfaction over a single binary relation R. The reader builds a sentence by clicking tiles (quantifiers forall/exists over x and y, the connectives and/or/not/implies, and the atoms R(x,y), R(y,x), R(x,x), R(y,y), x=y) which append in prefix order; the engine parses the prefix sentence to an abstract syntax tree and evaluates it on each of several small author-supplied structures (finite directed graphs), showing live which structures satisfy it. This is the symbolic-input modality the corpus otherwise lacks: you assemble a formula and watch the models split into satisfy / not. The renderer owns the tile palette, the prefix builder with backspace/clear, the well-formedness check, the FO evaluator (recursive over the AST and the finite domain), the per-structure satisfaction diagrams, and the readout; the structures are author-supplied. The gesture is 'compose-evaluate' — building a syntactic object and watching it evaluate. Pure DOM/SVG; jsdom-safe (no getScreenCTM/rAF; click-driven).

widgetId.description: DOM id for the outer <div class="widget"> wrapper. The tile / backspace / clear buttons derive their ids from it.

formulaId.description: DOM id for the <div> showing the formula being built.

svgId.description: DOM id for the <svg> drawing the structures + their satisfaction marks.

outputId.description: DOM id for the .readout (well-formedness / how many structures satisfy).

hint.description: Optional hint in .hd > .hint. Should tell the reader to click tiles to build a sentence.

svgTitle.description: Accessible <title> inside the SVG. Defaults to title.

structures.description: The finite directed graphs (sigma = one binary relation R) the sentence is evaluated on. Each {label, n (domain size 0..n-1), edges: [[i,j], ...]}.

n.description: Domain size; the domain is {0, 1, ..., n-1}.

edges.description: The pairs (i, j) with R(i, j) true.

presets.description: Optional starter sentences offered as one-click buttons. Each {label, tokens: [...] } where tokens are the prefix tile keys (Ax,Ex,Ay,Ey,AND,OR,NOT,IMP,Rxy,Ryx,Rxx,Ryy,EQ).
